items.question: Why should a kaula practitioner be worshipped as the supreme sacred place?
premises: kaula practitioner is supreme sacred place
therefore kaula should always be worshipped
items.inference: The practitioner himself becomes the highest tirtha, so constant worship of kaula is enjoined.
uncertainties: exact ritual referent of kaula worship remains context-dependent
items.plain_english: A kaula practitioner is the supreme sacred place, therefore one should always worship the kaula.

items.question: What benefit or result is absent for one who dwells in a kaula body through kaula worship?
premises: beings dwell in a kaula body
kaula worship is the source of benefit
items.inference: The verse implies that nothing desirable is lacking when kaula worship is performed in the kaula body.
uncertainties: whether the question is rhetorical or literal
items.plain_english: What would not be present for those dwelling in a kaula body through kaula worship?

items.question: Why is the kaula place called blessed, honorable, and most meritorious, sought by gods?
premises: that place is blessed and honorable
items.inference: The kaula place is exalted above ordinary places and desired even by divine beings.
uncertainties: whether deśa refers to physical place or practitioner
items.plain_english: That place is blessed, honorable, and most meritorious, and is sought by the gods.

items.question: Who on earth knows the power of one devoid of merit and sin?
premises: one is devoid of merit and sin
who knows that power on earth
items.inference: The verse highlights the rarity and transcendence of the power belonging to one beyond merit and sin.
uncertainties: whether vihīna means free from or lacking both
items.plain_english: Who on earth knows the power of one devoid of merit and sin?

items.question: How does the kaula wander on earth while teaching worldly conduct?
items.inference: The kaula remains active in the world, instructing ordinary conduct while moving through earthly life.
uncertainties: whether lokayātrā means worldly life or ritual conduct
items.plain_english: Teaching worldly conduct, the kaula wanders on earth.

items.question: What consecration procedure should be compassionately taught to the seeker?
premises: the speaker asks to hear it
items.inference: The verse requests compassionate instruction in the rite of consecration.
uncertainties: whether abhiṣeka refers to initiation or ritual bathing
items.plain_english: Out of compassion, cause me to hear the procedure of consecration.

items.question: How does secret performance of consecration lead to liberation and kaula status?
premises: consecration may occur night or day
items.inference: Secret or manifest consecration, performed according to ability, establishes kaula status and worship roles.
uncertainties: compound boundaries and exact sandhi unresolved
items.plain_english: Men formerly attained liberation by secret practice; consecration may be done night or day, manifestly or secretly; full consecration makes one a kaula, circle lord, and kula worshipper; the guru worships Vighnesha according to ability; and so forth for the fully consecrated kaula; night, at night.
